text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall-sre: Customer Monolith (private VPC) reports 502/504s from private endpoint behind NLB. Severity: P1. Links: https://console.redwood/incident/INC-2026-345

oncall-sre: I'm awake, grabbing context. Anyone see alerts in console?

alice: alert spiked around 12:14 UTC, target-group health shows 0/4 healthy for backend-targets in us-west-2b only. health check failing with ECONNRESET.

bob-net: I'm on network. Quick ask: is this NLB fronting EC2s in customer VPC or our private hosts?

carol-sre: It's Monolith private deployment (customer-managed hosts in their VPC). We see NLB->targets failing health checks. Customer reported no changes on their side initially.

dave-cs: Customer-netops (Monolith) pinged support: "sudden 502s to API in our private deployment, only affects traffic through NLB, internal services fine". I'm on the call with them.

customer-netops: Confirmed — we did not change SGs or ASG. We see failed health checks and some TCP resets. We'll run tcpdump if you need.

bob-net: Please run tcpdump on one of the affected hosts, filter for SYN/ACK and rst to NLB health-check ip. Example: ```sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.10.10.5 and port 80 -w /tmp/monolith-nlb.pcap```

alice: Ran curl from NLB health check IP (simulated): ```curl -v --connect-timeout 2 http://10.10.10.5:80/health``` Response: connection reset after tcp handshake.

carol-sre: I see recent kernel conntrack counters jumping on the host: `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` in dmesg on two hosts. Possible conntrack exhaustion due to NAT egress churn.

frank-sec: Did a rule audit — no new SG inbound rules. But customer has an egress-focused firewall appliance that started logging many ephemeral flows to external telemetry endpoints around the same time.

erin-soleng: Can we temporarily bypass the customer's forced egress NAT appliance by routing health checks via private peering to a dedicated health-check pool? Workaround idea: route NLB health checks to alternate target group pointing at our dedicated pool endpoints.

carol-sre: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) register fallback targets in the customer NLB target group pointing at our Dedicated pool NAT endpoints (we own) 2) set health-check matcher to 200 and interval to 10s, threshold 3 3) failover traffic via weights. Need customer consent for insertion of our targets.

customer-netops: We can add your dedicated targets to the target group, but need the exact IPs and we will apply via IaC. Provide IPs now.

alice: Sending ephemeral list: 10.20.30.12, 10.20.30.13 (dedicated health proxies). We'll also publish short-term SSH for validation.

bob-net: Before they add, note NLB target health checks originate from NLB internals; when we add our targets we must ensure they accept health check source IPs and TLS settings. If customer LB is internal-only, we need to ensure routing/SG egress permits 10.20.30.0/24.

carol-sre: Action: dave-cs + customer-netops to add targets and lower health check threshold. erin-soleng to set up proxy endpoints and validate responses. frank-sec to sign off SG changes. I'll coordinate traffic shift.

frank-sec: Quick note: we will only ask for inbound SG from NLB to those dedicated IPs. No broad open. We'll require narrow port/cidr and temporary 2-hour window.

customer-netops: Adding the two IPs to target group now via terraform. Apply in ~3 mins. Noted security window.

incident-bot: Deploy job started by erin-soleng: deploy/health-proxy-v2 -> staging -> prod (monolith fallback) (link)

erin-soleng: Proxy is up. Health endpoints return 200 with body `ok\n` on /health. Verified from our side: ```curl -s http://10.20.30.12/health``` -> ok

alice: Target registration shows NLB starting health checks. First results coming in...

alice: 10.20.30.12 -> healthy, 10.20.30.13 -> healthy. Customer LB showing 2/2 healthy now.

carol-sre: Initiating weight shift: reduce original target group weight by 90%, route new traffic to dedicated proxies. We'll gradually shift to avoid cache storms.

customer-netops: We're seeing successful requests now, errors trending down to <1%. Good so far.

dave-cs: Communicating to Monolith product team: "we've inserted temporary health proxies and shifted most traffic to them while you investigate conntrack exhaustion on your hosts".

carol-sre: Next steps (owner tags): alice -> collect conntrack dumps from impacted hosts; bob-net -> review NAT/gw config and long-lived ephemeral port usage; frank-sec -> review SG/IDS alerts; erin-soleng -> keep proxies healthy and prepare rollback plan; dave-cs -> coordinate customer comms and change ticket.

alice: Uploaded conntrack output to incident bundle: `/var/log/incident/1876543210/conntrack.txt` — shows ~260k entries, conntrack max is 262144. Looks like we hit ceiling. Temp mitigation: toss conntrack entries for dst IPs to free slots (not ideal).

bob-net: Customer reports a telemetry job started at 12:11 that opens tons of outbound flows (third-party analytics). Suggest they throttle or NAT pooling. We'll provide recommended iptables hints: ```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288``` and `conntrack -D --orig-dst 3rd.party.ip` but must do via change control.

customer-netops: We will throttle telemetry and schedule a kernel conntrack bump with our infra team. For now keep proxies in place.

carol-sre: Monitoring: errors down, latency normal. We'll keep in fallback for 2 hours, then attempt a controlled shift back after conntrack remediation. Set follow-up check in 45m.

frank-sec: Approving limited SG change. Documenting allowed CIDR and expiration in ticket.

incident-bot: Note: handoff reminder in 45 minutes to oncall-sre rotation.

(30m later)
oncall-sre: Handoff check-in: conntrack bump applied by customer, telemetry throttled. customer says no more rapid churn. How do we want to proceed?

carol-sre: Plan: 1) Reduce fallback weight to 20% for 10 minutes and observe 2) If health remains stable, remove fallback targets and return to standard NLB->customer-hosts 3) Keep probes and alerting tight. Anyone object?

bob-net: sounds good. Recommend a canary from a small subset of regions first (us-west-2b only).

erin-soleng: Scheduled automated rollback window in case things regress: `at now +25 minutes` will reapply fallback weights if errors > 2%

dave-cs: Notifying Monolith: "we will start shifting 80% back in 5 minutes. We'll pause if any error spikes."

customer-netops: Ready on our side. Go ahead 5m.

carol-sre: Starting weight shift to reduce fallback to 20% now.

alice: Observing health and logs... no immediate spikes. Error rate holds ~0.3%.

(10m later)

alice: After canary, all healthy. Proceeding to remove fallback targets from target group.

bob-net: Confirmed removal completed, NLB now points only at customer targets. Health checks green.

customer-netops: Confirmed stable from Monolith monitoring dashboards. Thanks for rapid support.

frank-sec: Closing security window and revoking temporary SG entries.

carol-sre: Incident summary (brief): Cause: conntrack table exhaustion on customer hosts caused by sudden telemetry job -> health checks failing -> NLB marked targets unhealthy. Mitigation: inserted dedicated health proxies into target group, shifted traffic, customer throttled telemetry and increased conntrack limit, validated stability, removed fallback.

dave-cs: Customer impact: ~18 minutes elevated error rate, no data loss reported, brief degraded UX for some API calls.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 resolved by carol-sre, severity downgraded to SEV2 at 13:05 UTC. Postmortem requested.

carol-sre: Assigning owners for postmortem: alice (root cause & logs), bob-net (network recommendations), erin-soleng (improvements to rapid fallback orchestration), dave-cs (customer comms draft). Please add notes to the incident doc.

customer-netops: We'll update our runbook to guard against conntrack exhaustion and add alerting for conntrack utilization. Thanks team. :tada:
